### Setup project and run tests

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/packages/bun-plugin-yaml/README.md

Install dependencies and execute the test suite when contributing to the plugin.

```bash
$ bun install # project setup
$ bun test # run tests
```

### Valid shortened import paths example setup

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/import/no-useless-path-segments.mdx

Demonstrates valid, simplified relative import paths in src/pages/home.js that are not reported.

```js
export function formatDate() {}
```

```js
export function Header() {}
```

```js
import { formatDate } from "../format.js";
import { Header } from "./header.js";
```

--------------------------------

### Setup logic in package.json bun-create section

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/templating/create.mdx

Specify pre- and post-install setup scripts in the "bun-create" section of a local template's package.json. preinstall and postinstall accept a string or an array of strings; arrays run in order. Commands run through the shell in the destination folder, and bun create stops with a non-zero code if a command or bun install fails.

```json
{
  "name": "@bun-examples/simplereact",
  "version": "0.0.1",
  "main": "index.js",
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^17.0.2",
    "react-dom": "^17.0.2"
  },
  "bun-create": {
    "preinstall": "echo 'Installing...'", // a single command
    "postinstall": ["echo 'Done!'"], // an array of commands
    "start": "bun run echo 'Hello world!'"
  }
}
```

### Example output when using .prettierrc with plugins

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/format/migrate-from-prettier.mdx

Shows how Bun reports which files are formatted natively and which are passed to your installed Prettier when a .prettierrc config includes plugins.

```txt
Using .prettierrc (Prettier config)

    3 files are formatted natively
    1 file goes to your installed Prettier: 1 *.astro

Built-in plugins: @ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports
Plugins that use your installed Prettier: prettier-plugin-astro

Still needed:   @ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports, prettier, prettier-plugin-astro (some files go to them)
```

### Install Bun in GitHub Actions with setup-bun

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/install/cicd.mdx

Use the official oven-sh/setup-bun action in a GitHub Actions runner step to install Bun and execute commands like bun install.

```yaml
name: my-workflow
jobs:
  my-job:
    name: my-job
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # ...
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 # [!code ++]

      # run any `bun` or `bunx` command
      - run: bun install # [!code ++]
```

--------------------------------

### Serve a file

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/trimmed-is-whole/cases/one-api-enters-the-code-of-another.js.txt

Starts a Bun server that returns a Response wrapping Bun.file('served.txt'), fetches it, logs the text, and stops the server.

```javascript
//@ file cwd/served.txt "from a file"
const server = Bun.serve({ port: 0, fetch: () => new Response(Bun.file("served.txt")) });
console.log(await (await fetch(server.url)).text());
server.stop(true);
```

--------------------------------

### Preload setup with bunfig.toml and setup.ts

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/suites-as-people-write-them/several-files.txt

Configures Bun to preload setup.ts before tests. setup.ts adds a custom matcher toBeUser, sets global fixtures, and defines beforeAll/afterEach hooks. Use to share setup across test files.

```toml
[test]
preload = ["./setup.ts"]
```

```typescript
import { afterEach, beforeAll, expect } from "bun:test";
console.log("setup is loaded");
(globalThis as any).fixtures = { users: ["ann", "bob"] };
expect.extend({ toBeUser(name: string) { return { pass: (globalThis as any).fixtures.users.includes(name), message: () => name + " is no user" }; } });
beforeAll(() => { console.log("before all"); });
afterEach(() => { (globalThis as any).fixtures.users.length = 2; });
```

--------------------------------

### Create HTTP server and make GET request with Node.js http module

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/trimmed-is-whole/cases/one-api-enters-the-code-of-another.js.txt

Starts an HTTP server on a random port, sends a GET request to /a, and logs the response body. Uses Node.js http module and server.close() to stop the server.

```javascript
const server = http.createServer((request, response) => response.end("from node " + request.url));
await new Promise(resolve => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
const body = await new Promise(resolve => http.get({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: server.address().port, path: "/a" }, response => { let all = ""; response.on("data", chunk => (all += chunk)); response.on("end", () => resolve(all)); }));
console.log(body);
server.close();
```

### Valid label references without whitespace

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/markdown/no-invalid-label-refs.mdx

These examples are not reported because they use valid label reference syntax: `[guide][]`, `[guide]`, and `[this][guide]`.

```markdown
Read the [guide][], the [guide], or [this][guide].

[guide]: https://example.com/guide
```

--------------------------------

### Set up toolchains and run homepage benchmarks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/bench/site/README.md

Sets up required toolchains and repositories, then executes the benchmark suite using a specified Bun binary under test. Supports running full suites, specific sub-benchmarks, or quick smoke tests via environment variables.

```sh
bench/site/setup-toolchains.sh                      # node, deno, pnpm/yarn/npm, bun release + canary -> $SITEBENCH_HOME/toolchains
bench/site/setup-repos.sh                           # rolldown/benchmarks clone + deps of bench/express, bench/websocket-server, bench/postgres
BUN=/abs/path/to/bun bench/site/run-all.sh          # everything: bundler http ws postgres install (~30 min with RUNS=3)
BUN=/abs/path/to/bun bench/site/run-all.sh http ws  # a subset
RUNS=1 BUN=... bench/site/run-all.sh                # quick smoke run
```

--------------------------------

### Serve a direct stream

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/trimmed-is-whole/cases/one-api-enters-the-code-of-another.js.txt

Starts a Bun server that returns a direct ReadableStream, fetches it, logs the text, and stops the server.

```javascript
const server = Bun.serve({ port: 0, fetch: () => new Response(new ReadableStream({ type: "direct", async pull(controller) { controller.write("one "); await controller.flush(); controller.write("two"); controller.end(); } })) });
console.log(await (await fetch(server.url)).text());
server.stop(true);
```

### Disallowed hook usage in test setup

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/vitest/no-hooks.mdx

An example of test setup using `beforeEach` that triggers a lint rule report.

```ts
import { beforeEach, expect, test } from "vitest";

let cart;

beforeEach(() => {
  cart = createCart();
});

test("starts empty", () => {
  expect(cart.items).toEqual([]);
});
```

### Install GCC 11 on Ubuntu with apt

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/project/contributing.mdx

Installs gcc-11 and g++-11. If the package cannot be located, add the ubuntu-toolchain-r/test PPA and run apt install again.

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install gcc-11 g++-11
# If the above command fails with `Unable to locate package gcc-11` we need
# to add the APT repository
sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:ubuntu-toolchain-r/test
# Now run `apt install` again
sudo apt install gcc-11 g++-11
```

### Install in production mode with bun install --production

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

Installs without devDependencies. --production implies --frozen-lockfile and only controls what gets installed; devDependencies already in node_modules remain. Use bun prune --production to remove them.

```bash
bun install --production
```

--------------------------------

### Valid test setup inside hooks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/bun-test/require-hook.mdx

Example of compliant test structure with setup logic placed inside `beforeAll` and `beforeEach` hooks.

```ts
import { beforeAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, mock, setDefaultTimeout, test } from "bun:test";

setDefaultTimeout(10_000);
mock.module("./mailer", () => ({ send: mock() }));

const names = ["ada", "grace"];
let db;

beforeAll(() => {
  db = connect();
  db.seed(names);
});

describe("users", () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    clearCache();
  });

  test("finds a user", () => {
    expect(db.find("ada")).toBeDefined();
  });
});
```

### WebSocket server and client

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/trimmed-is-whole/cases/one-api-enters-the-code-of-another.js.txt

Starts a Bun server with WebSocket upgrade and perMessageDeflate, connects a WebSocket client, sends a message, logs the echoed response, and closes.

```javascript
const server = Bun.serve({ port: 0, fetch(request, server) { return server.upgrade(request) ? undefined : new Response("no"); }, websocket: { perMessageDeflate: true, message(socket, message) { socket.send("echo " + message); } } });
const socket = new WebSocket(server.url.href.replace("http", "ws"));
const echoed = await new Promise(resolve => { socket.onopen = () => socket.send("ping ping ping ping"); socket.onmessage = event => resolve(event.data); });
console.log(echoed);
socket.close();
server.stop(true);
```

### Get nanoseconds since process start with Bun.nanoseconds()

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/utils.mdx

Returns the number of nanoseconds since the current bun process started, as a number. Useful for high-precision timing and benchmarking.

```ts
Bun.nanoseconds();
// => 7288958
```

```sh
bun --fetch-preconnect https://bun.com ./my-script.ts
```

### Start a simple HTTP server with Bun.serve

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/http/simple.mdx

Starts an HTTP server listening on port 3000 that responds to every request with status 200 and "Welcome to Bun!".

```typescript
const server = Bun.serve({
  port: 3000,
  fetch(request) {
    return new Response("Welcome to Bun!");
  },
});

console.log(`Listening on ${server.url}`);
```

### Example --explain output for unknown-object

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/compiler/explain.mdx

Sample output from `bun compile --explain` showing an unknown-object diagnostic at line 7, with notes about untyped access and a suggested fix.

```txt
7 | const saved: any = JSON.parse('{ "sku": "B-2", "price": 10 }');
                            ^
note: 1. unknown-object: The compiler doesn't know the shape of what JSON.parse() returns.
   at main.ts:7:25

note: 1 of 1 untyped access
note: 1 of these runs in a loop
note: used at main.ts:11:36
note: fix: check its fields and build a new object from them.
note: https://bun.com/docs/compiler/explain#unknown-object
```

--------------------------------

### Complete bunfig.toml test configuration example

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/test/configuration.mdx

Shows the available test configuration options, including test discovery, execution, coverage, and reporter settings. Install settings in [install] are inherited by tests.

```toml
[install]
# Install settings inherited by tests
registry = "https://registry.npmjs.org/"
exact = true

[test]
# Test discovery
root = "src"
preload = ["./test-setup.ts", "./global-mocks.ts"]
pathIgnorePatterns = ["vendor/**", "submodules/**"]

# Execution settings
smol = true

# Coverage configuration
coverage = true
coverageReporter = ["text", "lcov"]
coverageDir = "./coverage"
coverageThreshold = { lines = 0.85, functions = 0.90 }
coverageSkipTestFiles = true
coveragePathIgnorePatterns = [
  "**/*.spec.ts",
  "src/utils/**",
  "*.config.js",
  "generated/**"
]

# Advanced coverage settings
coverageIgnoreSourcemaps = false

# Reporter configuration
[test.reporter]
junit = "./reports/junit.xml"
```

### Compare esbuild and bun build CLI commands

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/esbuild.mdx

Shows the equivalent esbuild and bun build commands for bundling an entrypoint to an output directory. Bun bundles by default, so the --bundle flag is omitted.

# esbuild
esbuild <entrypoint> --outdir=out --bundle

# bun
bun build <entrypoint> --outdir=out
```

### Install with symlink backend and run with --preserve-symlinks

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/pm/cli/install.mdx

With --backend=symlink, Node.js won't resolve node_modules of dependencies unless each dependency has its own node_modules folder or you pass --preserve-symlinks to node or bun. The example installs with the symlink backend, then runs a file under bun and node with --preserve-symlinks.

```bash
rm -rf node_modules
bun install --backend symlink
bun --preserve-symlinks ./my-file.js
node --preserve-symlinks ./my-file.js # https://nodejs.org/api/cli.html#--preserve-symlinks
```

### Run shell commands with Bun Shell quickstart

Execute shell commands using the $ template tag and pass JavaScript objects like fetch Response instances directly into stdin.

```ts
import { $ } from "bun";

const response = await fetch("https://example.com");

// Use Response as stdin.
await $`cat < ${response} | wc -c`; // 1256
```

### Serve frontend with Bun.serve and HTML imports

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/src/runtime/cli/init/rule.md

Demonstrates setting up a full-stack server using Bun.serve with route handlers, WebSockets, HTML imports, and React/CSS bundling. Run index.ts using bun --hot for hot reloading.

```ts
import index from "./index.html"

Bun.serve({
  routes: {
    "/": index,
    "/api/users/:id": {
      GET: (req) => {
        return new Response(JSON.stringify({ id: req.params.id }));
      },
    },
  },
  // optional websocket support
  websocket: {
    open: (ws) => {
      ws.send("Hello, world!");
    },
    message: (ws, message) => {
      ws.send(message);
    },
    close: (ws) => {
      // handle close
    }
  },
  development: {
    hmr: true,
    console: true,
  }
})
```

```html
<html>
  <body>
    <h1>Hello, world!</h1>
    <script type="module" src="./frontend.tsx"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

```tsx
import React from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";

// import .css files directly and it works
import './index.css';

const root = createRoot(document.body);

export default function Frontend() {
  return <h1>Hello, world!</h1>;
}

root.render(<Frontend />);
```

```sh
bun --hot ./index.ts
```

});

--------------------------------

### New-or-call pattern

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/perf/everyday/downleveled.txt

Constructor returns a new instance if called without new. The prototype has a get method.

```typescript
function V(this: any, x: number): any {
  if (!(this instanceof V)) return new (V as any)(x);
  (this as any).x = x;
}
V.prototype.get = function () { return this.x + 1; };
function turn(i: number): number {
  return (V as any)(i & 7).get();
}
```

### Babel createClass with getter

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/perf/everyday/downleveled.txt

Babel-transpiled class using _createClass and _classCallCheck. The get method returns this.x + 1.

```typescript
  function V(this: any, x: number) { _classCallCheck(this, V); this.x = x; }
  return _createClass(V, [{ key: "get", value: function get(this: any) { return this.x + 1; } }]);
})();
function turn(i: number): number {
  return new V(i & 7).get();
}
```

--------------------------------

### ArrayBufferSink.prototype.start(options?)

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/runtime/streams.mdx

Configures and starts the sink with buffer allocation and streaming options.

```APIDOC
## start(options?)

### Description
Initializes the internal buffer and streaming settings for the sink.

### Syntax
```ts
sink.start(options?: {
  asUint8Array?: boolean;
  highWaterMark?: number;
  stream?: boolean;
}): void;
```

### Parameters
- **options** (object) - Optional configuration object.
  - **asUint8Array** (boolean) - Optional. If set, output is returned as a `Uint8Array`.
  - **highWaterMark** (number) - Optional. Preallocates an internal buffer of this size to improve performance with small chunk sizes.
  - **stream** (boolean) - Optional. On `flush()`, returns written data as `Uint8Array` / `ArrayBuffer` and restarts writes from the beginning of the buffer.

### Return Value
- `void`
```

### Import and use node:http createServer and fetch

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/trimmed-is-whole/cases/built-in-modules.js.txt

Starts an HTTP server on a random port, fetches it, then closes the server.

```javascript
import http from "node:http";
const server = http.createServer((request, response) => response.end("ok"));
await new Promise(resolve => server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
console.log(await (await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}/`)).text());
server.close();
```

### Implement a custom Bun plugin

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/fullstack.mdx

Create a plugin that exports a BunPlugin object with a name and setup function. The example loads .custom files as JavaScript modules.

```typescript
import type { BunPlugin } from "bun";

const myPlugin: BunPlugin = {
  name: "my-custom-plugin",
  setup(build) {
    // Plugin implementation
    build.onLoad({ filter: /\.custom$/ }, async args => {
      const text = await Bun.file(args.path).text();
      return {
        contents: `export default ${JSON.stringify(text)};`,
        loader: "js",
      };
    });
  },
};

export default myPlugin;
```

--------------------------------

### onStart

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/bundler/plugins.mdx

Registers a callback that runs when the bundler starts a new bundle. The callback may return a Promise, and the bundler waits until all onStart callbacks have completed before continuing.

```APIDOC
## onStart

### Description
Registers a callback that runs when the bundler starts a new bundle. The callback can return a Promise; after the bundle process has initialized, the bundler waits until all `onStart()` callbacks have completed before continuing.

### Signature
```ts
onStart(callback: () => void | Promise<void>): void;
```

### Parameters
- **callback** (function) - Required - A function that runs when the bundler starts a new bundle. May return `void` or `Promise<void>`.

### Notes
- `onStart()` callbacks (like every other lifecycle callback) cannot modify the `build.config` object. To mutate `build.config`, do so directly in the `setup()` function.

### Example
```ts
await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ["./app.ts"],
  plugins: [
    {
      name: "onStart example",
      setup(build) {
        build.onStart(() => {
          console.log("Bundle started!");
        });
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

### Example (async callbacks)
```ts
const result = await Bun.build({
  entrypoints: ["./app.ts"],
  outdir: "./dist",
  sourcemap: "external",
  plugins: [
    {
      name: "Sleep for 10 seconds",
      setup(build) {
        build.onStart(async () => {
          await Bun.sleep(10_000);
        });
      },
    },
    {
      name: "Log bundle time to a file",
      setup(build) {
        build.onStart(async () => {
          const now = Date.now();
          await Bun.$`echo ${now} > bundle-time.txt`;
        });
      },
    },
  ],
});
```
```

--------------------------------

### Generic Box class

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/perf/everyday/kinds-of-types.txt

`Box<T>` stores a value of type `T` and `get(): T` returns it; instantiated here as `Box<number>`.

```typescript
class Box<T> { constructor(public value: T) {} get(): T { return this.value; } }
const boxes: Box<number>[] = [new Box(1), new Box(2), new Box(3), new Box(4)];
function turn(i: number): number {
  return boxes[i & 3].get() + 1;
}
```

### Legacy decorator implementations in routes.ts

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/suites-as-people-write-them/one-file.txt

Defines Get, Named, Max, and Arg decorators using experimental decorators. Get wraps methods and records routes; Named adds a label; Max clamps a property; Arg records argument index.

```typescript
export const routes: string[] = [];
export function Get(path: string) { return (target: any, key: string, descriptor: PropertyDescriptor) => { routes.push(path + ":" + key + ":" + target.constructor.name); const original = descriptor.value; descriptor.value = function (...all: unknown[]) { return "[" + path + "]" + original.apply(this, all); }; }; }
export function Named(name: string) { return <T extends new (...all: any[]) => object>(type: T) => class extends type { label = name; }; }
export function Max(limit: number) { return (target: any, key: string) => { const kept = new WeakMap<object, number>(); Object.defineProperty(target, key, { get() { return kept.get(this) ?? 0; }, set(n: number) { kept.set(this, Math.min(n, limit)); }, enumerable: true }); }; }
export function Arg(target: any, key: string, index: number) { routes.push("arg" + index + key); }
```

### Create and run a new Elysia project using bun create

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/elysia.mdx

Initialize a new Elysia application in Bun, enter the project directory, and start the development server with hot reloading.

```bash
bun create elysia myapp
cd myapp
bun run dev
```

--------------------------------

### API server setup with beforeAll and afterAll

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/test/lifecycle.mdx

Start a test server in beforeAll and stop it in afterAll so it is available across the test run.

```typescript
import { beforeAll, afterAll } from "bun:test";
import { startServer, stopServer } from "./server";

let server;

beforeAll(async () => {
  // Start test server
  server = await startServer({
    port: 3001,
    env: "test",
  });
});

afterAll(async () => {
  // Stop test server
  await stopServer(server);
});
```

--------------------------------

### Install dependencies and run benchmark suites

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/bench/README.md

Run benchmarks directly from the bench directory after installing required benchmark dependencies such as mitata. Specify a custom runtime binary by setting environment variables like BUN or modifying the .env file.

```bash
# run from this directory. bench/ has its own package.json and bun.lock,
# the repo root does not install benchmark dependencies such as mitata.
bun install

bun run ffi
bun run log
bun run gzip
bun run async
bun run sqlite

# to use custom version of bun/deno/node binary
BUN=path/to/bun bun run ffi
# or edit .env file
```

--------------------------------

### Serve static files with Bun.serve

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/http/stream-file.mdx

Implement a basic static file server by combining Bun.file with Bun.serve.

```typescript
// static file server
Bun.serve({
  async fetch(req) {
    const path = new URL(req.url).pathname;
    const file = Bun.file(path);
    return new Response(file);
  },
});
```

### Escape block quote marker for literal setext heading

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/bun/md/spec.txt

Use backslash escapes when literal text starting with a block quote marker is intended as a setext heading.

```example
\> foo
------
.
<h2>&gt; foo</h2>
```

### Autolink URLs with paths

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/js/bun/md/spec-permissive-autolinks.txt

Matches optional URL paths starting with '/' and delimited by slashes. Non-alphanumerical characters (., -, _) in path components must be bounded by alphanumerical characters.

```example
https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png
.
<p><a href="https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png">https://example.com/images/branding/logo_272x92.png</a></p>
.
--fpermissive-url-autolinks
```

### Install express with bun add

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/deployment/render.mdx

Install the Express library into the project using Bun package manager.

```sh
bun add express
```

### Add start script to package.json

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/guides/ecosystem/tanstack-start.mdx

Adds a start script to package.json to run the custom server script with Bun alongside the build script.

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "bun --bun vite build",
    "start": "bun run server.ts" // [!code ++]
  }
}
```

### Reported URL examples with default "never" option

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/docs/lint/rules/unicorn/relative-url-style.mdx

Demonstrates code reported under the default "never" style when URLs start with `./`.

```js
const logo = new URL("./logo.png", import.meta.url);
const icon = new URL(`./${name}.svg`, import.meta.url);
```

### Two native ES6 classes

Source: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/blob/main/test/aot/perf/everyday/downleveled.txt

Defines two ES6 classes V and W with get methods and a turn function that instantiates them.

```typescript
class V { x: number; constructor(x: number) { this.x = x; } get(): number { return this.x + 1; } }
class W { y: number; constructor(y: number) { this.y = y; } get(): number { return this.y + 2; } }
function turn(i: number): number {
  return new V(i & 7).get() + new W(i & 3).get();
}
```
